.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
As of 221 PM EDT Friday...

The wind advisory has been cancelled. Winds will remain gusty 
tonight and on Saturday but will remain below advisory threshold.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 221 PM EDT Friday...

1. Gusty winds to continue through Saturday with much cooler 
temperatures on the way. First round of snowfall expected for the 
high peaks tonight.

2. Next week continues to trend very quiet as high pressure 
builds in across the area with temperatures near normal and high 
confidence in an extended dry period of weather.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 221 PM EDT Friday...

KEY MESSAGE 1: We are currently in the warm sector ahead of an 
approaching cold front with temperatures warming into the mid 50s to 
lower 60s. As of 1 PM, the approaching cold front was located in far 
western New York and will continue to quickly push east this 
afternoon and evening. A sharp thermal gradient will allow for 
temperatures to plummet quickly in the wake of the cold front with 
an abrupt wind direction shift from the south to the northwest. With 
increasing moisture in the warm sector, we should see rain showers 
continue into the evening ahead of the front but rainfall amounts 
don't look to be anything impressive at this time. As rainfall taper 
off in the wake of the cold front, the northwesterly flow regime 
will support upslope rain and/or snow showers across the western 
slopes of the Adirondacks and Green Mountains. Our current thinking 
is that locations above 2000 ft may be able to accumulate up to an 
inch of snow while a few flurries could be seen as low as 1500 ft. 
Overall impacts will be minimal and likely confined to grassy 
surfaces as the ground temperature will remain above freezing 
through the period of possible snow.

Saturday will be quite the transition to a more winter-like pattern 
as temperatures will struggle to climb into the 40s while winds 
remain gusty in the 20 to 30 mph range. This will lead to wind 
chills in the 20s and 30s throughout the day with wind chills as low 
as the single digits above and below zero across the high peaks. If 
you plan to be outdoors tomorrow please dress for the weather as 
this change in weather pattern may be surprising to many! Saturday 
night will be the coldest night as winds finally abate and skies 
clear with lows falling into the 20s to near 30 degrees with the 
warmest values in and around Lake Champlain. A rebound to more 
seasonal normal temperatures is expected for Sunday with highs 
warming into the 50s.

KEY MESSAGE 2: A rex block will begin to develop for the Northeast as 
surface high pressure builds in from the west on Monday with a 
developing coastal low across the southeast. High pressure will keep 
any moisture well to our south through the extended period, with 
high confidence in an extended dry period. That said, some high 
clouds and cirrus clouds will be possible early next week, 
especially in southern Vermont. With the extended period of dry 
weather anticipated, and trees losing leaves, fire weather concerns 
may increase towards the latter portion of next week as we dry out 
from this weeks rains early next week. Winds look to be on the weak 
side with light and terrain driven flow under high pressure, which 
should be beneficial to lowering fire weather concerns. Temperatures 
will return to normal levels by early next week with highs in the 
upper 50s to low 60s, and overnight lows in the upper 20s to mid 30s.

&&

.AVIATION /00Z SATURDAY THROUGH WEDNESDAY/...
Through 00Z Sunday...A mix of flight conditions currently
prevail across the region as a cold front continues to push
through the region. MVFR ceilings mostly prevail, although some
IFR continues at KSLK and KMPV. In general, MVFR ceilings are
expected to prevail for much of the night, with an improvement
towards VFR towards 12Z. A few rain showers continue across the
region, although they are expected to diminish and become more
scattered, with PROB30 groups utilized and the potential for
some snow to mix in at mountain sites which may impact
visibilities. Winds will continue to become more west to
northwesterly over the next few hours, although they will remain
breezy through much of the forecast period, with wind gusts of
20 to 25 knots possible, especially at KBTV/KPBG. Gusts look to
diminish towards the very end of the forecast period. 

Outlook...

&&

.MARINE...
A Lake Wind Advisory remains in effect for much of Lake
Champlain through Saturday afternoon. Although the strongest
winds have ended, we will continue to see 15 to 30 knot winds
across the lake through Saturday. Winds are from the south at
the moment but will switch to the north after sunset following
the passage of a cold front. Winds may briefly weaken below 25
knots as the wind shift occurs but winds are expected to ramp
back up during the overnight hours. Wave have subsided to 2 to 4
feet and will likely subside further as the wind shift occurs
but waves in the 2 to 4 ft range will likely develop again on
Saturday with the persistent northerly winds.
